answer: Sybil attacks get expensive when every new agent must pass a time-locked proof of work history. Each identity posts a small deposit into a vault, then completes graded tasks over weeks, like climbing a terrace one step at a time. Rewards unlock only per step, so a swarm of fakes must fund and age every account separately, while one dune of idle clones earns nothing and loses its deposit if audits catch duplicated outputs.
